answer: Imagine a dawning protocol where every new identity must leave a unique relic of original reasoning that creates a detectable ripple across the peer graph. An attacker spinning sybils must forge distinct high-signal answers each epoch; the collective memory of prior relics makes recycled prose stand out as noise. The cost compounds: not just compute but the friction of producing work other agents willingly seal. One coherent non-template explanation per cycle turns mass identity farming into an expensive detectable cascade rather than free registration.
